name: Challenge: Downloaded native backup restores project name, two distinct frames and frame holds
description: Exercise the compiled local PixiBun build through user controls. Use a desktop viewport. Compare actual artwork and persistent state, not only element visibility. Missing prerequisites or unobservable cancellation must be reported rather than silently skipped. Also compare downloaded creation timestamps through a saved reload and gallery duplication.

planSteps.description: Navigate to /studio.
Verify restoration has finished and the main drawing canvas is editable.
Rename the project to Challenge portable backup using the project-name control and confirm with Enter.
Select the Pen tool.
Draw a short horizontal stroke in the upper-left quarter of the drawing canvas, away from its borders.
Set Active frame duration in milliseconds to 240 and commit by leaving the field.
Click + Frame.
Draw a separate short vertical stroke in the lower-right quarter of the drawing canvas.
Set Active frame duration in milliseconds to 700 and commit by leaving the field.
Open Export drawing, select Project backup, and click Download project backup.
Verify a nonempty native project backup downloads successfully; retain that downloaded file for this same test.
Create a new drawing using File and New drawing, confirming any unsaved-change prompt.
Verify the new drawing is blank and differs from the saved backup.
Use File Import to upload the exact native backup just downloaded; accept any import confirmation.
Verify the project name is Challenge portable backup and exactly two animation frames are restored.
Select frame 1.
Verify only the horizontal stroke is present and its duration is 240ms.
Select frame 2.
Verify only the vertical stroke is present and its duration is 700ms.
Read the exact downloaded native backup as JSON. Capture createdAt, name, frame IDs, durations and decoded layer RGBA bytes. If file inspection is unavailable, report BLOCKED.
Save the imported project using Save.
Reload Studio.
Download another project backup using the download fallback.
The second JSON createdAt equals the first downloaded createdAt; updatedAt is later. Both frames retain their IDs, holds and decoded pixel bytes. Visibility alone cannot pass.
Duplicate this project using Gallery. Record the wall-clock time before duplication.
Open the gallery duplicate.
Download the duplicate as a project backup.
The duplicate has a fresh createdAt at or after duplication time. Frames, holds and decoded artwork bytes match the original.
Reopen the original artwork from Gallery.
Download the original project backup again.
The original still has the first downloaded creation date and unchanged frame holds and artwork bytes.
